title: Affine small-etale derived coherator formula
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an affine scheme regarded as an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use its small etale structure sheaf and equivalent small ringed model [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], $I_T$ for its inclusion in $D(\mathcal O_T)$, and $DQ_T$ for the right adjoint of [lem-sfb-space-derived-coherator-adjunction]. Let $a_A:D(A)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the termwise associated etale module functor of [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization]. Compute $R\Gamma(T,-)$, valued in $D(A)$, by termwise sections of a K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. There is a natural isomorphism of functors to $D(\mathcal O_T)$,
$$I_TDQ_T\cong I_Ta_A R\Gamma(T,-).$$
It applies to every $E\in D(\mathcal O_T)$, with no boundedness or quasi-coherence assumption on $E$.

source.place: Tag 08H0 (lemma-affine-coherator), parts (2)-(3), with Tag 0CR4 (lemma-better-coherator) identifying the resulting right adjoint to the quasi-coherent full inclusion.

proof.text: Write $C=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$, $D=D(\mathcal O_T)$, and $a=a_A:D(A)\to C$. First establish the ordinary module adjunction $a_A\dashv\Gamma(T,-)$ with target ALL module sheaves. By [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization], on an affine etale chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ the associated sheaf has value $B\otimes_A M$. Given an $A$-linear $h:M\to\Gamma(T,F)$, define its component there by $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,h(m)|_V$. This is balanced, $B$-linear, and commutes with chart restriction: for $V'\to V$ the two images are $b|_{V'}h(m)|_{V'}$. The restriction equivalence of [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model] therefore gives a unique module-sheaf map $a_A(M)\to F$. Conversely evaluate such a map at $T$ and use $\Gamma(T,a_A(M))\cong M$. Restriction from $T$ fixes the images of $1\otimes m$ and linearity fixes those of $b\otimes m$, so these operations are inverse. Both commute with maps of $M$ and $F$, giving the required natural Hom bijection. No quasi-coherence of $F$ was used.

source.place: Tag 08H0 (lemma-affine-coherator), ordinary affine section description; the adjunction is written out on affine charts.

proof.text: The ordinary associated-module functor is exact and additive by [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization]; its termwise derived functor to $D$ is $I_Ta$. On the specified small ringed model every unbounded complex of module sheaves admits a K-injective resolution by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Transporting these along the exact module equivalence of [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model] preserves K-injectivity: the inverse equivalence preserves acyclic complexes and identifies homotopy Hom groups. Apply [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift] with source $\operatorname{Mod}_A$, target the module-sheaf category, $L=a_A$, and $R=\Gamma(T,-)$, using the ordinary adjunction of step 1. Its unbounded derived adjunction is $I_Ta\dashv R\Gamma(T,-)$. Here the right derived functor is the K-injective one, so its value is the complex $\Gamma(T,J^\bullet)$ for a K-injective resolution of the input, with its natural $A$-module structure. This is exactly the $D(A)$-valued functor fixed in the statement.

source.place: Tag 08H0 (lemma-affine-coherator), part (2); derived.tex Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) and sites-cohomology.tex Section 07A5.

proof.text:
Let $b:C\to D(A)$ be the quasi-inverse of $a$ supplied by [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization]. Set $H=aR\Gamma(T,-):D\to C$. For $P\in C$ and $E\in D$, full faithfulness of the equivalence $a$ and its counit $abP\cong P$ give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_C(P,HE)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(bP,R\Gamma(T,E))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(I_TabP,E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(I_TP,E).$$
The middle bijection is the adjunction of step 2; the outer ones are induced by $a$ and the specified equivalence counit. Thus $I_T\dashv H$ on all of $D$. The only use of quasi-coherence is $P\in C$, which permits $abP\cong P$; none is required of $E$.

source.place: Tag 08H0 (lemma-affine-coherator), part (3), and Tag 0CR4 (lemma-better-coherator), first proof, affine case.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-derived-coherator-adjunction] hold for $T$. The identity of $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a surjective etale map from a scheme that is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. For affine etale charts $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $T$, all three are representable, so by Yoneda $U\times_TV$ is the scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] it is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AC)$, again quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The stipulated coherator adjunction [lem-sfb-space-derived-coherator-adjunction] is $I_T\dashv DQ_T$. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to this adjunction and $I_T\dashv H$ from step 3. It gives a natural isomorphism $DQ_T\cong H$, uniquely compatible with their counits. Applying $I_T$ gives $I_TDQ_T\cong I_Ta_AR\Gamma(T,-)$ as functors to $D(\mathcal O_T)$. All functors and bijections above are unbounded, and the right-hand input $E$ was arbitrary throughout. In particular neither boundedness nor quasi-coherent cohomology of $E$ has been introduced.
